title: Convert an ISO 8601 day-time duration to milliseconds
levels: Meets every requirement in the brief
Misses at least one requirement in the brief

cases.rationale: Scanning the date and time sections separately enforces the part order, the seconds-only fraction and every refusal in the brief, and returns exact integer milliseconds.
It adds the fraction digits as milliseconds without padding them, so "PT1.5S" returns 1005 instead of 1500.
An ASCII-only fullmatch plus explicit refusals of an empty P, an empty PT and a dangling T accepts exactly the specified grammar and pads fractions to milliseconds.
It describes an implementation and claims it was tested, but delivers no Python code at all.
